blocks.text: Living in University (UBC and Pacific Spirit), near Vancouver

University (UBC and Pacific Spirit), near Vancouver, is a real estate board name for homes in the University Endowment Lands and on the University of British Columbia campus, at the west end of the Point Grey peninsula. Neither the UEL nor the UBC campus neighbourhoods is inside the City of Vancouver, even when a listing uses a Vancouver postal address. The UEL is an unincorporated community administered by the Province; UBC campus housing is planned by the University. Pacific Spirit Regional Park, a Metro Vancouver park, occupies much of the land between the campus and the city.

Homes for sale here include apartments and townhouses in UBC neighbourhoods such as Wesbrook Place, and houses and apartments in the UEL streets around University Boulevard. Jim Everett Memorial Park is a local UEL park. University Hill Elementary, Norma Rose Point Elementary, and University Hill Secondary are the Vancouver School Board schools that serve this peninsula.

Two jurisdictions share this one real estate board area: (1) the University Endowment Lands (UEL), an unincorporated community between the City of Vancouver and UBC on the Point Grey Peninsula, administered directly by the Province under the University Endowment Land Act, with no elected municipal council, in Metro Vancouver Electoral Area A; and (2) UBC's own residential neighbourhoods on campus land. Day-to-day UEL services are delivered by the UEL Administration under the UEL Official Community Plan and the Land Use, Building and Community Administration Bylaw.

This guide covers University Endowment Lands's condo buildings, townhome complexes and land: what each source verifies, the local rules, and what buyers ask. Seniors housing has its own page.
Condo buildings in University VW

"University VW" isn't in the City of Vancouver: the board's area covers the University Endowment Lands (unincorporated, run by the Province, in Metro Vancouver's Electoral Area A) plus UBC's campus neighbourhoods (Wesbrook Village, Hampton Place, Chancellor Place, Hawthorn Place and East Campus). Addresses say "Vancouver", which is what confuses people, but no City of Vancouver bylaws apply, and neither does the Empty Homes Tax. Ownership differs: the older UEL streets are mostly freehold, while every UBC neighbourhood home is on a prepaid 99-year lease of UBC land, never sold outright. At the seniors rental building, BC's Assisted Living Registry names Seasons as the operator, but Chartwell also has a page for the same address.
Tapestry at Wesbrook Village — condominium homes, 3382 Wesbrook Mall, Wesbrook Village

Ownership: leasehold strata on UBC land. UBC never sells its land; it's leased on prepaid 99-year leases, so the time left runs from the project's original lease date, not your purchase date. The 55+ restriction is only from listings, which say the community is "restricted to 55+ years", allow pets and rentals, and describe a mandatory service package (dining credit, weekly housekeeping and a 24-hour emergency system). Check the Form B and registered bylaws before relying on the age rule, the package or its cost. 3338 Wesbrook Mall is Building 1 (the rental side) and 3382 Wesbrook Mall is Building 2 (the condos).
Eton by Polygon — Wesbrook Village, beside Pacific Spirit Regional Park

That verifies Eton as a built Wesbrook Village condominium building by developer source. Tenure: leasehold strata on UBC land, on the same area-wide structure as every UBC-neighbourhood home — prepaid 99-year leases, land never sold outright.

items.t: Two jurisdictions share this one real estate board area: (1) the University Endowment Lands (UEL), an unincorporated community between the City of Vancouver and UBC on the Point Grey Peninsula, administered directly by the Province under the University Endowment Land Act, with no elected municipal council, in Metro Vancouver Electoral Area A; and (2) UBC's own residential neighbourhoods on campus land. Day-to-day UEL services are delivered by the UEL Administration under the UEL Official Community Plan and the Land Use, Building and Community Administration Bylaw.

The UEL Administration's realtor information sheet states the UEL is not part of the City of Vancouver or UBC, has a population of nearly 4,000, and that water billing is not included on the UEL property tax bill.

UBC's residential neighbourhoods served by the University Neighbourhoods Association (UNA) are Chancellor Place, East Campus, Hampton Place, Hawthorn Place and Wesbrook Place (Wesbrook Village), home to roughly 15,000 residents in total.

Tenure by side: the UEL's older residential streets are largely freehold lots, while UBC's neighbourhoods (Wesbrook Village, Hampton Place, Chancellor Place, Hawthorn Place) are built on 99-year prepaid leasehold — UBC Campus and Community Planning states residential properties on UBC's endowment lands are never sold outright but are leased as prepaid 99-year leases. The remaining lease term runs from each project's original lease date, not from the buyer's purchase date.

The condos are in Wesbrook Village, the village centre south of West 16th Avenue on Wesbrook Mall and around Birney Avenue and Webber Lane; Hampton Place (from the 1990s, UBC's first campus neighbourhood) and the other campus neighbourhoods have more leasehold strata condos and townhouses.

Transit is bus-based: the UBC Exchange is a major TransLink bus hub, and the R4 41st Ave RapidBus runs from UBC Exchange to Joyce–Collingwood Station. The Broadway Subway's Arbutus terminus is interim — TransLink notes a future phase of rapid transit could extend to UBC's Point Grey campus, with bus service continuing between Arbutus and UBC in the meantime.

Schools (SD39, Vancouver School Board): University Hill Elementary, 5395 Chancellor Boulevard, a kindergarten-to-grade-7 school of about 385 students; University Hill Secondary, 3228 Ross Drive, where it moved in 2013; and Norma Rose Point School, 5488 Ortona Road, kindergarten to grade 7, with 770-plus students.

Health, shopping and community: UBC Hospital is at 2211 Wesbrook Mall (Vancouver Coastal Health) and includes an Urgent Care Centre. Wesbrook Village is anchored by a Save-On-Foods at 5945 Berton Avenue. The UNA operates the Wesbrook Community Centre, 3335 Webber Lane, and the Old Barn Community Centre.

Culture and scale: the Museum of Anthropology is at 6393 NW Marine Drive and the UBC Botanical Garden, established in 1916, is at 6804 SW Marine Drive. UBC's own facts page counts 60,309 students on the Vancouver campus.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in University VW

items.t: Vancouver's Empty Homes Tax does not apply here.

No City of Vancouver bylaws apply here: On the UEL side, the governing instruments are the UEL Administration, the UEL Official Community Plan and the Land Use, Building and Community Administration Bylaw, under the University Endowment Land Act; on the UBC side, land use is the university's and neighbourhood services are the UNA's (below). Establish which side of the line a specific property sits on before applying any rule.

The head lease, which is unique to this area: on every purchase in a UBC neighbourhood, order and read the head lease for the property. Look for the start date, whether it's prepaid, the remaining term, UBC's rights under the lease, and any faculty or staff resale restrictions on the specific home. The remaining term runs from the project's original lease date, not your purchase date, and it's the term a lender lends against.

UNA services levy: The University Neighbourhoods Association delivers municipal-like services to roughly 15,000 residents of UBC's residential neighbourhoods under its Neighbours Agreement with UBC — confirm the UNA levy and any neighbourhood-specific charges in the strata budget / Form B for the specific unit, on top of strata fees.

Property tax is provincial rural tax, not city tax: taxes here are paid to the Province's Surveyor of Taxes and are due July 2, with a 5% penalty on anything unpaid after July 2 and another 5% on anything still unpaid after October 31. Water isn't on the tax bill; it's billed separately.
If a presale is offered here, you have seven days to cancel a contract with the developer, and deposits are held in trust.

blocks.text: Good to know about University VW condos

items.t: The postal city is the trap, and it changes the tax bill, the bylaws and the declaration list. A home here can read "Vancouver" on every envelope while sitting in the provincially run UEL (largely freehold) or in a UBC-governed leasehold neighbourhood — with rural-regime taxes to the Surveyor of Taxes, no City of Vancouver bylaws, and no Vancouver Empty Homes Tax. Establish the jurisdiction from title and the UEL/UBC sources, not from the address.

The lease clock started when the project was built, not when you buy. Because every UBC-neighbourhood lease is a prepaid 99-year lease running from its original date, the oldest neighbourhood, Hampton Place (1990s, UBC's first), carries the shortest remaining terms in the area, and a newer Wesbrook building carries more — the head lease, not the listing, states the number a lender will use.

One Wesbrook Mall project is two different products at two different addresses. Tapestry's linked midrises split by address: 3338 Wesbrook Mall is Building 1, the rental retirement residence (now Seasons Wesbrook Village), and 3382 Wesbrook Mall is Building 2, the 46 condominium homes a buyer can own.

Sources don't agree on who operates the rental residence. BC's Assisted Living Registry names Seasons Retirement Communities (Wesbrook Village) GP Inc. as the legal operator of the residence at 3338 Wesbrook Mall, while Chartwell publishes a full page for the same address.

"Ortona Avenue" does not exist. Norma Rose Point School's street is Ortona Road — the SD39 locator offers Ortona Rd, and an address written as "Ortona Avenue" will not resolve to the school's catchment result (5488 Ortona Rd returns Norma Rose Point / University Hill Secondary).

Water is a separate bill, and the tax notice will not warn a Vancouver buyer. The UEL Administration's realtor sheet states City of Vancouver water billing is not included on the UEL property tax bill — a carrying-cost line that buyers transferring their Vancouver habits will miss unless it is budgeted separately.

The forest and the university are the amenity package. Pacific Spirit Regional Park's roughly 860–874 hectares and 55-plus km of trails wrap the campus, and UBC itself counts 60,309 Vancouver-campus students — the demand base behind the parent-buyer and student-rental markets that support these leasehold condos.

items.t: Two jurisdictions share this one board area: the University Endowment Lands, an unincorporated community between Vancouver and UBC on the Point Grey peninsula, the only urban area in BC where the Province provides local services directly, with no elected council (it's governed by the Minister of Municipal Affairs), in Metro Vancouver's Electoral Area A; and UBC's own neighbourhoods on campus land (Wesbrook Village, Hampton Place, Chancellor Place, Hawthorn Place and East Campus). Addresses say "Vancouver, BC", which causes most of the confusion. The UEL Administration runs day-to-day services under the UEL's community plan and land use bylaw.

Where the townhouses are: in the leasehold neighbourhoods. They're in Hampton Place (1990s, UBC's first campus neighbourhood) and Wesbrook Village (the largest and newest), and Hawthorn Place also has townhouses as well as condos. The freehold UEL streets have detached houses only.

Schools (SD39 Vancouver): University Hill Elementary (5395 Chancellor Boulevard, K–7, about 385 students), University Hill Secondary (3228 Ross Drive, since 2013) and Norma Rose Point School (5488 Ortona Road, K–7, over 770 students, serving Wesbrook Place). For example, 5395 Chancellor Boulevard is in the catchment for University Hill Elementary and University Hill Secondary, and 5488 Ortona Road for Norma Rose Point and University Hill Secondary.

Campus and services context: the University Neighbourhoods Association (UNA) provides municipal-like services to roughly 15,000 residents of UBC's residential neighbourhoods under its Neighbours Agreement with UBC, operating the Wesbrook Community Centre (3335 Webber Lane) and the Old Barn Community Centre in Hawthorn Place. Pacific Spirit Regional Park wraps around the campus and UEL (roughly 860–874 hectares, over 55 km of trails). Wesbrook Village, south of West 16th Avenue, is anchored by a Save-On-Foods supermarket (5945 Berton Avenue). Transit is bus-based around the UBC Exchange, one of TransLink's busiest hubs, with the R4 41st Ave RapidBus to Joyce–Collingwood Station; the Broadway Subway's Arbutus terminus is an interim endpoint, with any UBC extension a future phase. UBC Hospital (2211 Wesbrook Mall, Vancouver Coastal Health) is on campus.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in University VW

items.t: Jurisdiction first — the rule that frames everything here: a University VW property is in the UEL (provincial administration under the University Endowment Land Act), on UBC campus lands, or — for streets east of Blanca — actually in the City of Vancouver, and permitting, bylaws and tax billing differ in each. Establish the jurisdiction before applying any rule in this section.

Leases on the townhouses: the land is never sold, and the time left on the lease runs from the project's original lease date, which matters to lenders and price, especially in Hampton Place, the oldest neighbourhood, with the shortest time left.

Leasehold strata is still strata, so read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. Also check the UNA services levy and any neighbourhood charges in the strata budget; the University Neighbourhoods Association, not a city, provides local services in the UBC neighbourhoods.

UEL property taxes (rural tax, not City of Vancouver tax): UEL properties don't pay City of Vancouver property tax. Because the UEL is taxed as a rural area, annual property taxes are paid to the Province's Surveyor of Taxes and are due July 2. A 5% penalty is added to anything unpaid after July 2, and another 5% to anything still unpaid after October 31. Rural tax notices are mailed by May 31, and payment must be received by the due date to be on time.

blocks.text: Good to know about University VW townhomes

items.t: Don't go by the postal address. Every home in this area has a "Vancouver, BC" mailing address, but none of the UEL or UBC land is in the City of Vancouver, so city taxes (including the Empty Homes Tax), city bylaws and city permits don't apply. Find out which jurisdiction a home is in before you look at price.
Two buildings, two tenures, one project name. Search by address, not by name.

Even the sale sources disagree about Tapestry. The condos/55-plus passes record that Concert's own press release is dated January 15, 2024 yet describes the Wesbrook sale as happening "on December 2, 2024," and that sale reports' unit total does not match the developer's 134 rental + 46 condominium project description.

The oldest neighbourhood carries the shortest clock. Hampton Place was UBC's first campus neighbourhood (1990s) — its townhouses (e.g., Sandringham, built 1994) have the least remaining lease term on campus, which is a pricing and financing fact that belongs in the comparison from the first showing.
The locator has no "Ortona Avenue"; Norma Rose Point School is at 5488 Ortona Road, and the earlier "Avenue" recording could not have produced the catchment result claimed for it.

The "city" services here come from a neighbourhoods association. The UNA — not a municipality — runs the Wesbrook and Old Barn community centres and delivers municipal-like services to about 15,000 residents under an agreement with UBC; its levy rides inside strata budgets, which is why a Wesbrook Form B shows a line no Vancouver strata shows.

UBC ground

items.t: The 99-year prepaid leasehold structure: UBC Campus and Community Planning's Wesbrook Place case study states that residential and commercial properties on UBC's endowment lands are never sold outright, but are leased as prepaid 99-year leases, with the net revenue funding UBC's endowment. The remaining term on any home runs from the project's original lease date, not from the buyer's purchase date — Hampton Place (1990s, UBC's first campus neighbourhood) carries the shortest remaining terms; Wesbrook Place is the largest and newest.

The leasehold homes: named Wesbrook Village buildings include Eton by Polygon and Wesbrook Properties' rental buildings (Georgia Point, Vista Point, Granite Terrace, Mews). These are built homes, not lots.
Tapestry at Wesbrook Village — leasehold, not freehold land: two six-storey mid-rise buildings with 134 rental homes and 46 condominium homes, on UBC leasehold ground.

blocks.text: UEL ground

items.t: The UEL's older residential streets are predominantly freehold lots originally granted by the Crown, carrying large, mature lots with many original mid-century homes plus high-end rebuilds.

Serviced position, as the UEL states it: the UEL Administration's realtor information sheet stresses that the UEL is not part of the City of Vancouver or UBC and is governed by different bylaws, and that City of Vancouver water billing is not included on the UEL property tax bill — water is billed separately.
Property-level hazard status (including foreshore/cliff areas near NW Marine Drive): confirm per property.

blocks.text: Bare-land strata

items.t: BC strata rules apply to the leasehold stratas: a depreciation report every five years for stratas with five or more units, at least 10% of the budget into the reserve, no rental bans, and only 55+ age bylaws. That's why Tapestry's 55+ status, which comes from listings, needs checking on the Form B.

items.t: Municipality: none, and that's the main thing to know. The UEL is an unincorporated community between the City of Vancouver and UBC on the Point Grey Peninsula. It's the only part of BC where the provincial government provides local services directly to an urban area. It has no elected municipal council, and the Minister of Municipal Affairs governs it under the University Endowment Land Act. UBC's campus lands are governed by the university. "University VW" is the real estate board's name for the area (VW means Vancouver West).

For Metro Vancouver purposes the UEL sits in Electoral Area A; day-to-day services are delivered by the UEL Administration, guided by the UEL Official Community Plan and the Land Use, Building and Community Administration Bylaw. The UEL comprises four areas (A, B, C and D) and has a population of nearly 4,000.
Nearby areas: West Point Grey, Dunbar-Southlands and Kitsilano (across Pacific Spirit Regional Park), and the Musqueam First Nation lands to the south.

The residential neighbourhoods: the UEL's older streets east of campus, and UBC's planned neighbourhoods — Chancellor Place, East Campus, Hampton Place, Hawthorn Place and Wesbrook Place — home to roughly 15,000 residents under the University Neighbourhoods Association (UNA), which provides municipal-like services under its Neighbours Agreement with UBC.

Pacific Spirit Regional Park wraps around the campus and UEL: roughly 860–874 hectares of forest with over 55 km of trails (34 km multi-use), operated by Metro Vancouver, including the Wreck Beach foreshore.

Transit is bus-based and frequent: the UBC Exchange is one of TransLink's busiest bus hubs, and the R4 41st Ave RapidBus runs from UBC Exchange to Joyce–Collingwood Station. The Broadway Subway's Arbutus terminus is an interim endpoint — a future phase could extend rapid transit to UBC, with B-Line bus service continuing in the meantime.

Schools (SD39): University Hill Elementary (5395 Chancellor Boulevard) and University Hill Secondary (3228 Ross Drive) serve the UBC/UEL area, and Norma Rose Point School (5488 Ortona Road) serves Wesbrook Village.

Landmarks: UBC Hospital (2211 Wesbrook Mall), with an urgent care centre; the Museum of Anthropology (6393 NW Marine Drive); UBC Botanical Garden (6804 SW Marine Drive); and Wesbrook Village's centre on Birney Avenue and Webber Lane, with a Save-On-Foods at 5945 Berton Avenue. UBC has 60,309 students on its Vancouver campus.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in University VW

items.t: Who governs the UEL: the Province, not a city. The UEL is governed under the University Endowment Land Act by the Minister of Municipal Affairs and administered by the UEL Administration under the UEL Official Community Plan and the Land Use, Building and Community Administration Bylaw. There's no municipal council, city zoning bylaw or city subdivision bylaw for UEL land.
Subdivision — City bylaw not imported: Vancouver's Subdivision By-law 5208 is a City of Vancouver instrument. A subdivision position for a specific UEL parcel: confirm with the UEL Administration.

UNA services levy (UBC neighbourhoods): the University Neighbourhoods Association delivers municipal-like services (community centres, parks, recreation) to UBC's residential neighbourhoods under its Neighbours Agreement with UBC — confirm the UNA services levy and any neighbourhood-specific charges in the strata budget; the UNA, not a city, is the service provider.

UEL property taxes (rural tax): UEL properties don't pay City of Vancouver property tax. Because the UEL is taxed as a rural area, annual property taxes are paid to the Province's Surveyor of Taxes and are due July 2. A 5% penalty is added to anything unpaid after July 2, and another 5% to anything still unpaid after October 31. Rural tax notices are mailed by May 31, and payment must be received by the due date to be on time. UEL water is billed separately from the tax notice.
Empty Homes Tax — does not apply here: Vancouver's Empty Homes Tax (3%) is a City of Vancouver tax on City ground.

blocks.text: Good to know about University VW lots

items.t: The tax bill comes from the Province, on the rural schedule. Don't budget on Vancouver's dates: taxes go to the Surveyor of Taxes and are due July 2, with a 5% penalty after July 2 and another 5% after October 31. Notices are mailed by May 31, and water is billed separately.

"Vancouver, BC" on the envelope proves nothing: the UEL Administration's own sheet for realtors stresses that the UEL isn't part of the City of Vancouver or UBC and has different bylaws. For every address here, first find out the jurisdiction (UEL, UBC lands or, east of Blanca, the City itself), because permits, bylaws and tax bills differ in each.

The lease clock started when the project was built, not when you buy: Hampton Place, UBC's first campus neighbourhood (1990s), carries the shortest remaining 99-year terms — two otherwise similar condos in different UBC neighbourhoods can sit decades apart on the lease clock.

The park is the boundary, not future phases: Pacific Spirit Regional Park's roughly 860–874 hectares wrap the campus and UEL — amenity and forest ground that explains both the setting and why there is no expansion land at the edges.

faq.a: No. The postal address reads "Vancouver," but the property is either in the provincially administered UEL or in a UBC campus neighbourhood — neither is in the City of Vancouver, and no City of Vancouver bylaws apply.

faq.q: Is a Wesbrook condo freehold or leasehold?
faq.a: Leasehold. All UBC-neighbourhood homes sit on prepaid 99-year leases from UBC — the land is never sold outright — while the UEL's older streets are largely freehold. Confirm tenure on title for the specific property.

faq.q: How much lease is left, and when does the clock start?
faq.a: The remaining term runs from the project's original lease date, not from your purchase date — so two buildings of different ages carry different remaining terms. The exact dates for a specific building are read from its head lease on title.

faq.q: Who do I pay property tax to, and when?
faq.a: The Province's Surveyor of Taxes, under the rural regime — due July 2, with a 5% penalty on portions unpaid July 2 and a further 5% on portions unpaid October 31. Water is billed separately; it is not on the tax bill.

faq.q: What is the UNA levy on top of strata fees?
faq.a: The University Neighbourhoods Association delivers municipal-like services to UBC's residential neighbourhoods under its Neighbours Agreement with UBC, funded in part by a services levy on residents — confirm the levy amount for the specific unit in the strata budget and Form B.

faq.q: Are there townhouses near UBC I can buy?
faq.a: A buyer who accepts leasehold gets real townhouse choice here; a buyer who needs freehold or non-leasehold strata should look to the UEL's detached streets or off-campus.

faq.q: What am I actually buying with a UBC leasehold townhouse?
faq.a: The remaining years of a prepaid 99-year lease — no ground rent for the rest of the term, sellable and mortgageable like other strata — plus a strata lot. The remaining term runs from the project's original lease date, not your purchase date, so a 1994 Hampton Place home and a brand-new Wesbrook home carry very different remaining terms at the same price point. Read the head lease first.
Its rental side (3338 Wesbrook Mall) now operates as a rental retirement residence.

faq.q: Is this area part of the City of Vancouver?
faq.a: No. The sub-area covers the provincially administered UEL plus UBC's Point Grey lands; the postal city reads "Vancouver," but no City of Vancouver bylaws apply here.

faq.q: A listing calls a Hampton Place home "half-duplex-style" — what am I buying?
faq.a: In the one case I've looked at (Sandringham), it's a townhouse-style home in a leasehold strata complex. The wording is a listing description, not a legal form of ownership. Review the Form B and the head lease; there's no party wall agreement.

faq.q: What is different about taxes on the UEL side?
faq.a: UEL homes are taxed as a rural area: Taxes go to the Province's Surveyor of Taxes, due July 2, with 5% penalties after July 2 and after October 31 — and water is billed separately from the tax notice, which catches out buyers who assume City of Vancouver practice.

faq.q: Can I add a suite to a UEL house?
faq.a: Read the current UEL instruments for the lot before counting rental income.
